population: Only invented anonymous game agents and fabricated opportunities; no real politician/party, voter, or identifiable person
source: Controlled pseudo-random simulator generated in V8 with seed, outputs not borrowed from real politics
information_parity: Compare rules on identical synthetic event draws; no extra foresight or exposure labels in one contender
multiplicity: Four predetermined experiments and one software verification; no hypothesis significance claim from seeded toy model
classification: AB-R synthetic = formal/mechanistic within simulated world, not field science; AB-P = local engineering QA, not sociological validation
grades: N1/N2/N3 remain 0 unless independently justified; no new 2/3 permitted on synthetic outputs
question: Can per-opportunity normalization create incentive to omit difficult scheduled actions when agents maximize expected synthetic league points?
rivals: all available events is optimal under raw count
select-easy is optimal under observed rate
scheduled-denominator correction protects incentive but changes reward meaning
estimand: Expected reward maximizing under policy choices all 20 opportunities vs only four easy ones, Bernoulli p_easy=.85 p_hard=.4; compare 4 scoring functions, plus 500 independent simulated realization pairs for check; no human choice inference.
primary: difference E[score(cherry)-score(all)] by rule, selected opportunities and score variance
falsifier: observed rate does not prefer selective policy under assumed p; scheduled denominator does not prefer all
control: known oracle expected reward in fixed toy mechanism; compare empirical Monte Carlo to exact analytic expectations
cost: 2 strategies ×500 random worlds; fixed assumptions not claims about political engagement.
